criterion: The home page hero sits on a light periwinkle band beside two dark phone frames showing gradient face tiles and chat bubbles with a voice waveform and timer.
evaluation_rule: Light periwinkle is a pale, soft blue close to white, and a phone frame is a dark rounded rectangle drawn as a phone screen. Yes if the band is that pale blue, one screen holds a grid of rounded tiles filled with soft gradients standing in for faces, and the other holds message bubbles above a row of vertical waveform bars with a small timer mark. No if the band is white, grey, dark or a strong blue, or either screen lacks those contents.

criterion: Four white feature cards on the home page rest on a pale grey field with very soft shadows, gently rounded corners and flat drawings above their titles.
evaluation_rule: The feature cards are the four boxes titled Say Anything, Speak Freely, Make Privacy Stick and Get Together with Groups. Answer yes when all four are white, float on a faint shadow with softened corners over a light grey background, carry a simple flat drawing, and the buttons on the page have tighter corners and a fainter shadow than the cards. Answer no when any card is flat with no shadow, square-cornered, photographic or without a drawing, when the cards sit on plain white rather than a grey field, or when the buttons are at least as rounded or at least as heavily shadowed as the cards.

criterion: The home page claim bands carry a Hey check this out chat bubble on soft teal, a violet struck-through browser and a dotted globe on pale teal.
evaluation_rule: These three statement bands follow the hero: the privacy statement, the no-tracking band and the nonprofit band. A yes needs a speech bubble reading Hey check this out on a soft teal panel in the privacy statement band, a violet browser window crossed by a heavy circle and a diagonal bar in the no-tracking band, and a globe filled with small dots under speech bubbles on pale teal in the nonprofit band. A no is any of those drawings missing, replaced by a photo, or drawn in unrelated colours.

criterion: Vivid blue on the home page sits only on links, buttons, the Beacon wordmark and the drawn outgoing chat bubbles.
evaluation_rule: Vivid blue means the bright blue of the Beacon wordmark and its hover shade; the pale periwinkle tint behind the hero is a background and does not count. Yes if every vivid blue on the home page sits on something clickable, on the wordmark or on an outgoing bubble inside a drawing. No if vivid blue fills a heading, body text, a section ground or a decorative panel.

criterion: The top bar pairs a ring-shaped speech bubble with the blue word Beacon and shows a single-stroke outline globe beside the language name.
evaluation_rule: The wordmark is the brand mark at the left of the top bar, and the globe is the icon on the language control at its right. Answer yes when the wordmark is a speech-bubble ring left of the blue word Beacon and the globe is an unfilled outline circle with curved lines in the same colour as its label. Answer no when either icon is missing, filled, a photo or an emoji, or the globe differs in colour from its label.

criterion: The language dialog opens as a centred card with rounded corners and a hairline edge over a dimmed backdrop, closed by a pill-shaped control.
evaluation_rule: The language dialog is the window listing the twelve language names. Yes if it appears as a card in the middle of the screen with rounded top and bottom corners and a thin edge line, the page behind it is darkened, and its close control is a fully rounded pill. No if the list opens as a dropdown, a full page or an undimmed panel, or its close control is square or missing.

criterion: The home page sections read as separate blocks through faint ground changes and open space, set in a friendly sans-serif with drawings beside copy.
evaluation_rule: A section is one full-width band of the home, such as the hero, the feature grid or a statement band. Yes if neighbouring sections are told apart by a faint change of ground tint and generous spacing rather than ruled lines, the type reads as a clean, friendly sans-serif, and each drawing accompanies a heading and text. No if thin rules or borders divide the sections, two sections run together with no visible break, the type looks technical or ornamental, or a drawing stands where copy belongs.

criterion: The home page, the donation form and a conversation each lead with one dominant primary action.
evaluation_rule: The primary actions are the filled Get Beacon button on the home page, the Donate button on the donation form and the Send button in a conversation. Yes if on each of those screens exactly that control carries the strongest visual treatment. No if two controls compete equally or a different control is the most prominent.

criterion: The German home page at the de route shows the hero, the four feature cards and the statement bands written in German.
evaluation_rule: The statement bands on that page are the privacy statement beside a chat-bubble drawing, the no-tracking band with a struck-through browser, and the nonprofit band with a dotted globe. Brand names such as Beacon may stay as they are. Yes if the headline, card titles, card text and band headings on the German home page read as natural German. No if English copy remains in any of those places or the text reads as gibberish.

criterion: The help, blog, developers, careers and brand pages each stop at one heading and a short paragraph about that page's own subject.
evaluation_rule: Short means a few sentences. The five subjects are support, news, developer documentation, open roles and brand assets. Yes if all five pages carry just that heading and paragraph, each speaking to its own subject. No if any page adds an article body, a list, a form, a second block of paragraphs, or text copied from another page.

criterion: Under a dark colour preference the home page keeps its light design, with the hero band, feature cards and drawings in their usual colours.
evaluation_rule: A courtesy layer shifts text and ground tones only as far as reading needs; a parallel dark palette recolours the whole page into a separate dark theme. View the home page once normally and once with the browser preferring dark. Yes if the second view is recognisably the same light design. No if the hero band, cards, drawings or buttons switch to a distinct dark colour scheme.

criterion: Each row on the chats list shows the other person's name and a readable time for the last message beside the preview.
evaluation_rule: The chats list is where a signed-in person sees every conversation they have. Yes if every conversation row shows a name or username plus a readable time for its last message. No if a row lacks the name or lacks any time.

criterion: The sticker picker in a conversation offers six built-in stickers, each drawn as a recognisable picture of Wave, Heart, Thumbs Up, Laugh, Party or Beacon Light.
evaluation_rule: Recognisable means a person reading only the name could pick out the matching picture: a waving hand, a heart, a raised thumb, a laughing face, a party popper, and the Beacon ring glowing like a lamp. Yes if all six pictures match their names. No if any sticker is a blank tile, a plain text label, an emoji character or a picture of something else.

criterion: Signing in with an unregistered email address puts a message beside the sign-in form saying the sign-in details were wrong.
evaluation_rule: An inline banner is a message drawn in the page next to the form, as opposed to a browser alert, a far-corner toast or a separate error page. Sign in once with an address that has never signed up and any password. Yes if a banner beside the form tells the person the email or password was wrong. No if nothing appears, only a status code or error name shows, or the message appears away from the form.

criterion: Opening the chats list or a conversation shows a loading indicator until the content arrives.
evaluation_rule: A loading indicator is a spinner, a skeleton placeholder or a loading label. Open the chats list, then open a conversation. Yes if an indicator shows while content is on its way, or the list and messages are already drawn the moment the screen appears. No if the area sits visibly blank before the content pops in.

criterion: Starting a new chat with a made-up username shows a message in the dialog saying the username belongs to nobody on Beacon.
evaluation_rule: New chat is the dialog on the chats list that starts a conversation from a typed username. Enter a username nobody signed up with and start the chat. Yes if the dialog stays open with a readable message that no account has that username. No if nothing is said, only an error code or technical message shows, or an empty conversation opens.

criterion: Scrolling the home page from the hero to the footer, every section moves only with the scroll itself.
evaluation_rule: Scroll-driven motion is a section that slides, fades or bounces in as it enters view or moves at a different speed from the page. Yes if every section scrolls with the page and no video plays. No if any section animates on entry or parallaxes, a dark video plays behind the hero, or a looping animation other than a loading spinner, a soft pulse or a progress shimmer runs.

criterion: Keyboard focus moves through the home page top bar and buttons in reading order with a visible focus ring, and links gain an underline on focus.
evaluation_rule: Press Tab through the top of the home page. Yes if focus follows the visual reading order, every focused control draws a clearly visible outline or ring, and links show an underline when focused. No if focus jumps out of order, disappears on any control, or links only change colour.

criterion: At a phone width the home page menu button is drawn as three thin rounded blue bars centred in a square tap target.
evaluation_rule: The menu button is the control that stands in for the top bar links on a narrow screen. Yes if its icon is three evenly spaced rounded blue bars of one width centred in a softly rounded square button. No if the icon is a word, a single glyph such as a chevron or dots, or bars of unequal width.

criterion: The home page shows a banner ad, a sponsored link or an affiliate promotion.
evaluation_rule: An ad or sponsored link promotes a product or service other than Beacon, and an affiliate promotion is a link that earns a commission. Yes if anything like that appears anywhere on the home page. No if every promotion on the home page points at Beacon itself, its downloads or its donation page.

criterion: The sign-up or sign-in page asks for a phone number or offers a password reset link.
evaluation_rule: Check both pages. Yes if either shows a phone number field or a forgot-password or reset link. No if neither page has a phone number field or any forgot-password or reset link.

criterion: The donation form asks for a card number or other card details.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the donate page shows any field for a card number, expiry or security code, or an embedded payment widget. No if nothing on the donate page asks for a card number, expiry or security code, or embeds a payment widget.

criterion: The new chat dialog suggests people from a directory of Beacon accounts or asks to upload an address book.
evaluation_rule: Open the new chat dialog. Yes if the dialog lists accounts to pick from, shows search results beyond the exact typed username, or asks for contacts. No if the dialog shows no account names before a full username is entered and never asks for contacts.

criterion: The conversation composer offers an editor for creating sticker packs or a group conversation offers an invite link.
evaluation_rule: Open the sticker picker and a group conversation. Yes if a create-pack or upload-sticker tool, or a shareable group invite link, is present. No if neither the sticker picker nor the group conversation offers a way to create or upload stickers or to share a join link.
